what_it_does: Optical neural networks use beams of light rather than electrical signals to perform AI computations, offering potentially huge gains in speed and energy efficiency because light can propagate through many channels in parallel without generating heat the way electrons do. One promising design — a diffractive optical neural network — encodes computation in the way a patterned optical surface bends and scatters light, but the pattern is fixed when the surface is manufactured, making it impossible to update for new tasks. CHORD combines such fixed free-space optics with a layer of reconfigurable integrated photonics (chip-scale optical switches that can be tuned after fabrication), and trains both the fixed and tunable components together so the system as a whole can learn new functions. This hybrid approach aims to get the massive parallelism of free-space optics while recovering the flexibility that diffractive-only designs lack.
